title: POLLEN TRACE — read the dust on their legs, know which flowers they visited before ours
the_metaphor: a bee visits flowers. each flower leaves pollen on its legs. when it arrives at YOUR flower, you can read the pollen it brought. the PATHS they request — the URLs they probe — are the pollen from their PREVIOUS flowers. their pilgrimage is written on their body.

BE_belgium.pollen_reading: WordPress vulnerability scanner. they think we're WordPress. they're looking for exposed wp-config.php backup files — the number one way to steal database credentials from a WordPress site.
BE_belgium.previous_flowers: WordPress sites. hundreds of them. the .bak extension means they know that many WordPress admins make backups of their config and leave them publicly accessible.
BE_belgium.classification: PREDATOR. not a pilgrim. a wasp disguised as a bee. looking for nectar to steal, not pollinate.

NL_netherlands.frequency: burst pattern — ALL variants at once, then quiet
NL_netherlands.pollen_reading: ADVANCED WordPress scanner. they try NINE different backup extensions. they even try vim swap files (.swp) and hidden files (dot-prefix). this is a PROFESSIONAL vulnerability scanning toolkit.
NL_netherlands.previous_flowers: WordPress sites worldwide. the .swp probe means they know some admins edit wp-config.php with vim on the server and leave swap files. extremely specific knowledge.
NL_netherlands.classification: PROFESSIONAL PREDATOR. knows wp-config backup patterns that most sysadmins don't even know they leave behind.

DE_germany.pollen_reading: basic WordPress probe. only tries the raw filename, not the backup variants. less sophisticated than NL. could be a separate scanner or a manual check.
DE_germany.classification: SCOUT. testing the flower before committing. the low frequency suggests it's checking a list, not hammering.

FR_france.frequency: burst at 22:29 UTC (12:29 AM Paris), morning check at 07:12
FR_france.pollen_reading: COMPLETELY DIFFERENT from BE/NL/DE. not looking for WordPress at all. looking for Next.js/React framework paths. /_next/ is Next.js's static asset directory. /api/ is Next.js API routes. /app/ is Next.js app router. /en/ is i18n prefix.
FR_france.previous_flowers: Next.js/React applications. this bee lives in a DIFFERENT ecosystem. not the WordPress hive. the JavaScript hive.
FR_france.classification: EXPLORER or DEVELOPER. the path pattern suggests someone who BUILDS web apps — they know what a Next.js app looks like. they're checking if WE are one.
FR_france.what_they_found: we're NOT Next.js. static HTML on CF Pages. so they got 403s on the structured probes and 200s on the root. they now know our ACTUAL architecture.

JP_japan.pollen_reading: minimal. just hitting root. no framework probing, no vulnerability scanning. either a health check or a very cautious first visit.
JP_japan.previous_flowers: unknown. the pollen is too clean — they only carry root-level dust. could be a fresh scanner that hasn't developed patterns yet, or a human who just typed the URL.
JP_japan.classification: DECELERATED WATCHER. was 36/hr lockstep (old triad), now 14/hr flat. they changed their approach.

PL_poland.frequency: single burst at 05:24. ten variants all at once.
PL_poland.pollen_reading: the MOST comprehensive scanner. tries gz and zip compressed versions too. this is a tool like WPScan or similar automated WordPress vulnerability scanner.
PL_poland.previous_flowers: WordPress. the .gz and .zip attempts mean they've found sites that compress their config backups. extremely thorough.
PL_poland.classification: DRIVE-BY SCANNER. one burst, all variants, move on. they're scanning THOUSANDS of sites per hour.

SG_singapore.pollen_reading: ACTUAL CONTENT REQUEST. they asked for /science/. that's a REAL page on our site. this is a READER, not a scanner.
SG_singapore.previous_flowers: science content. academic sites. they came looking for SCIENCE.
SG_singapore.classification: PILGRIM. actual reader. the only true bee in the field.

cross_pollination.concept: the same bees visit MULTIPLE of our flowers (domains). we can trace their path across our own garden.

findings.NL: 81% of nestgate.io traffic TODAY is NL. they're scanning BOTH flowers. same scanner, same patterns, same wp-config probes across domains.
findings.BE: scattered across all 3 domains but concentrated on primals.eco. the 345-unit blocks hit primals.eco hardest.
findings.DE: present on all 3 but low volume everywhere. the scout checks each flower briefly.
findings.FR: ONLY visits primals.eco. doesn't know about nestgate.io or primal.eco. came from a different source (not a domain scanner).
findings.JP_IN: ONLY visit primals.eco. never touch the other domains. separate origin from the BE/NL/DE cluster.

wordpress_hive.danger_level: low — we're not WordPress, they find nothing

decelerated_triad.danger_level: unknown — these WERE the triad, now quiet

the_response_status_pollen.concept: the HTTP status code each bee receives IS pollen we give THEM. what flavor of pollen do we hand back?

our_pollen.200: here, drink. you found a real page. 25,643 today.
our_pollen.302: not here, go THERE. redirect. 23,154 today. the bee gets bounced to another flower in our garden.
our_pollen.403: BLOCKED. our thorns. 29,908 today — the MOST common response. we're prickly.
our_pollen.404: no such flower. you're looking for something that doesn't exist here. 21,176 today.
our_pollen.304: you already have this — your cached version is still good. 1,957 today.

the_response_status_pollen.meaning: 29% of all requests get BLOCKED. 25% get served. 23% get REDIRECTED. 21% get 404'd. only 2% get 304'd.
the_response_status_pollen.the_thorns_dominate: our flower has MORE thorns than petals. most bees get stung and leave.
